newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end mixed despite Wall Street rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end mixed despite Wall Street rise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mixed despite momentum from Wall Street's big rebound overnight, as the market was trapped in caution by concerns over typhoon damages and upcoming cabinet reshuffle, brokers said.

The weighted index, buoyed by Dow Jones industrial average's 1.4-percent rise on Monday, climbed to an intra-day peak of 9,806.29 in early session but lost steam in late trade to finish only 5.88 points or 0.06 percent to 9,712.45.
Turnover was relatively light at T$117.63 billion.
The Dow's rise on Monday helped it regain almost half of Friday's 247-point decline.
"Investors are feeling a bit cautious because of Wall Street's recent big movements," said Lin Long-hsien, analyst for United Securities.
"The typhoon and the expected cabinet reshuffle later this week are all mild bearish factors," Lin said.
Typhoon Winnie swept through northern Taiwan on Monday and Tuesday, killing at least 25 people and causing landslides that toppled numerous buildings.
Although electronics gained 0.30 percent on Wall Street's rose, constructions fell 0.43 percent reflecting infrastructure damages caused by the typhoon.
Pao-Ku Co tumbled by its daily seven-percent limit or T$2.80 to T$37.50.
"Any time after a typhoon ravages the island, the stock market will not be in a cheery mood," Lin said.
Brokers said they did not expect the index to gain significant upside room until after the government launched its expected cabinet reshuffle later this week.
A 9,650-9,800 range was seen for Wednesday.
